references.text: Jacob's blessing promises that 'Shiloh' will come – a messianic prophecy pointing to the expected Messiah. The Samaritans knew this prophecy and awaited a coming figure who would declare all things. [ref: Gen 49:10|Genesis 49:10]

Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like himself, and the people should listen to him. The Samaritans, who recognized only the books of Moses, especially awaited this prophet – 'Taheb' – as the Messiah who would 'declare all things to us'. [ref: Deut 18:15-18|Deuteronomy 18:15-18]
Daniel's prophecy about 'an anointed one, a prince' who will come is a central messianic text that supports the expectation of the Messiah (χριστός, 'the Anointed'). [ref: Dan 9:25-26|Daniel 9:25-26]

Andrew says to Simon Peter: 'We have found the Messiah' – the same title used by the Samaritan woman. John translates both instances of the Hebrew 'Messiah' into the Greek 'Christ' (χριστός). [ref: John 1:41|John 1:41]
Jesus answers directly to the woman's statement about the Messiah with his 'I am' – he confirms himself that he is the Messiah she awaits. [ref: John 4:26|John 4:26]

After speaking with Jesus, the woman goes to the town and says: 'He told me everything I have done. Could this be the Messiah?' – a direct fulfillment of her expectation that the Messiah would 'declare all things to us'. [ref: John 4:29|John 4:29]
The Samaritans confess that Jesus is 'the Savior of the world' – they have come to believe in him as the Messiah the woman spoke about. [ref: John 4:42|John 4:42]

Many in the crowd believed in Jesus and said: 'When the Messiah comes, will he do more signs than this man has done?' – the same messianic expectation that characterizes the Samaritan woman's words. [ref: John 7:31|John 7:31]

Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will 'guide you into all truth' and 'declare to you what is to come' – a fulfillment of the expectation that the Messiah would 'declare all things to us' (ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα). [ref: John 16:13|John 16:13]
